newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says to keep watching forex, mindful of G7.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says to keep watching forex, mindful of G7.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will continue to watch movements in the foreign exchange market keeping in mind cooperation with Group of Seven (G7) nations, BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.

Asked whether an agreement to cooperate in foreign exchange markets reached by the G7 nations in a meeting earlier this month meant there would be coordinated intervention, Matsushita said nothing concrete had been decided in advance.
"It will depend on our decision, to be made by watching market movements," he said.
"I will decline to comment on intervention, but we will continue to watch market movements, keeping in mind the cooperation (with other G7 nations)," he added.
Matsushita said the G7 nations agreed that misalignment in the foreign exchange market noted in the G7"s April 1995 communique had been corrected.
"Exchange rates should move in accordance with this agreement and reflect economic fundamentals. It is desirable that the rates move in a stable manner," he said.
He also said the yen"s weakening had accelerated a rise in prices of imports into Japan and added that the central bank needed to watch domestic prices carefully.
But he said domestic prices did not show any signs of moving into a clear rising trend, as supply and demand conditions in the Japanese economy had improved only moderately.

He said: "The weak yen has speeded up the tempo of the rise in prices of imports, and we need to carefully watch domestic prices from now on. But domestic prices do not show signs of moving into an upward trend, and there is little possibility that they will, as the improvement in supply and demand conditions remains moderate."
